solutions.explanation:
15 is \(30\%\) of 50. Since \(30\%=\frac{30}{100}\), this means \(15\div50=\frac{30}{100}\). Multiplying the quotient by \(100\) gives
\[
15\div50\times100=\frac{30}{100}\times100=30.
\]
solutions.title: Use the percentage relationship

solutions.explanation:
Multiplication and division have equal priority, so evaluate from left to right. First \(15\div50=0.3\). Multiplying by \(100\) moves the decimal point two places to the right, so
\[
15\div50\times100=0.3\times100=30.
\]
solutions.title: Compute the decimal quotient, then multiply by 100
